findings.description: The invite code is the only secret that grants workspace membership, but it is generated with `random.choices`, which uses the Mersenne Twister. Its output is predictable once enough outputs are observed, so an attacker who sees a few codes could predict others and join workspaces.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `"".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))`.
findings.title: Invite codes generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `accept` rejects revoked or exhausted links, but never checks `now >= link.expires_at`. An expired link can still be used to join the workspace, so the TTL is not enforced. `is_active(now)` already encodes the full rule and is not used here.
findings.title: accept() does not check link expiry
